# 6.1 CWM SIG 
This section tests trait-environment relationships using a Community Weighted Mean significance test (CWM.Sig) based on permutations. Two permutational approach is considered here:

- taxa.shuffle;

- trait.shuffle.

```{r}
rm(list = ls()) ## Clear the R environment to ensure a clean workspace

library(SYNCSA)          # For ecological analysis, includes CWM and null models
library(openxlsx)        # Reading/writing Excel files
source("func/cwm_sig.txt")         # Custom function for CWM significance testing
source("func/summarize_trees.R")   # Custom script, possibly for summarizing phylogenetic trees
library(tidyverse)       # For data manipulation and visualization
library(readxl)          # Reading Excel files

runs = 9999              # Number of permutations for the null model
options(scipen = 9999)   # Avoid scientific notation in outputs

```

## Load data 

```{r}
# Community data (species abundance per site)
d <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = "w_matrix")

# Create community matrix (sites x taxa), aggregating species counts
w_matrix <- reshape2::acast(
  site ~ taxa,
  data = d,
  value.var = "FA_New",
  fun.aggregate = sum
) %>%
  round(digits = 2) # Round to two decimal places

# Environmental data
e_matrix <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = "e_matrix") %>%
  dplyr::filter(Site %in% rownames(w_matrix)) %>%       # Match only relevant sites
  column_to_rownames('Site')                         # Set site names as rownames
 

# Trait data
t_matrix <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = "t_matrix")
head(t_matrix)

# Binarization of categorical variables
rhiz_type <- table(t_matrix$taxa, t_matrix$rhizome_type)         # Rhizome type as binary table
morph <- table(t_matrix$taxa, t_matrix$frond_morphology)         # Frond morphology as binary table

# Check alignment of taxa for trait matrix construction
t_matrix[match(rownames(rhiz_type), t_matrix$taxa), ]
t_matrix$laminae_pubescence

# Create trait matrix (species x traits) with continuous and binarized traits
t <-
  cbind.data.frame(
    diam = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$rhizome_diameter,
    r_comp = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Compact"],
    r_cr = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Short-Creeping"],
    r_lr = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Long-Creeping"],
    lmseg = t_matrix[order(order(t_matrix$taxa)), ]$laminae_dissection,
    ltri = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$laminae_pubescence,
    buds = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$proliferous_buds,
    ind = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$indusium,
    ldim = morph[order(rownames(morph)), 'Dimorphic'],
    chl = t_matrix[order(order(t_matrix$taxa)), ]$spore_chlorophyll
  ) %>%
  filter(rownames(.) %in% colnames(w_matrix)) # Filter to include only species present in w_matrix

dim(t)
head(t)
glimpse(t)
```
### Load models

```{r}
nice_mods <- read.xlsx('outputs/cwm_raw_results.xlsx', sheet = 3) # List of relevant models
cwm_values <- readRDS("data/cwm_values_raw.RDS")                  # Raw CWM values
```
### Organizing data 

```{r}
org_data <- organize.syncsa(w_matrix, traits = t, envir = e_matrix) # Format data for analysis
saveRDS(file = "data/org_data.RDS", org_data)                       # Save for reproducibility

mem <- readRDS(file = 'outputs/RDS/mem_chl_traw.RDS')              # Load MEM variables for spatial structure
```

## CWM SIG Testing

Each model tests a trait against environmental predictors using permutation-based null models.

```{r}
nice_mods

rdiam <- get_cwm(
  comm = org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = diam ~ ann_prec * prec_seas + samp_size + plot_size,
  runs = runs,
  model = T
)


rcomp <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = r_comp ~ nitrogen + samp_size + plot_size,
  runs = runs
)

screep <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = r_cr ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

buds <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = buds ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

ind <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = ind ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

dim <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = ldim ~ ann_prec + prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

lmseg <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = lmseg ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

spore <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = chl ~
    ann_prec *
      prec_seas +
      mem$selected.MEM$MEM5 +
      mem$selected.MEM$MEM1 +
      plot_size +
      samp_size,
  runs = runs
)
```

## Output data 

```{r}
# Combine all CWM significance results into a single data frame
cwm.results <-
  full_join(rcomp$cwm.sig, screep$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(rdiam$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(lmseg$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(buds$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(ind$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(dim$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(spore$cwm.sig)

# View only significant results (p-value < 0.05)
cwm.results[cwm.results$ts < 0.05, ]

# Combine model data for further plotting or correlation analysis
p <- cbind(
  rdiam$model$data,
  rcomp$model$data,
  screep$model$data,
  lmseg$model$data,
  buds$model$data,
  ind$model$data,
  dim$model$data,
  spore$model$data
)

# Remove duplicated columns
df <- p[!duplicated(as.list(p))]

# Example correlation between two traits
cor(df$r_cr, df$lmseg)

```
### Save data

```{r}
write.xlsx(
  x = list(results = cwm.results, plots = df),     # Save both results and model data
  "outputs/cwm_sig_traw.xlsx",                     # Output path
  startRow = 1,
  startCol = 1,
  keepNA = T,                                       # Keep missing values
  rowNames = T                                      # Include row names
)
```
